reviews.title: Makes tracking fun!
reviews.text:
I’ve tried several calorie and nutrition tracking apps, including some that are arguably more minimal or streamlined, but YAZIO is the one I actually enjoy using consistently. The interface is easy to understand, the food tracking works well, and I really appreciate that features like activity calories and water tracking can be adjusted or turned off depending on how you prefer to track.

What really sets YAZIO apart for me is the sense of fun. The mascot, animations, streaks, diamonds, chests, and rewards make logging food feel much less tedious and give me a reason to keep coming back to the app. It feels encouraging without making nutrition tracking feel clinical or boring.

I also like the food database, the overall design, and the flexibility of the Pro version. I know some people prefer a completely stripped-down tracker, but for me the gamification is exactly why this app works better than others I’ve tried. It turns consistency into something I actually look forward to.

If you’re someone who wants a nutrition app that is both useful and genuinely enjoyable to use, YAZIO is absolutely worth trying.

reviews.title: Great core app, but too many pop-ups and limited AI
reviews.text:
I generally like YAZIO, but the constant pop-ups and repetitive coaching messages are becoming really annoying. I don’t need to be told for the 25th day in a row that adding protein powder to my breakfast is a good source of protein. I understood it the first few times.

For a while I managed to get these messages to stop, but now they suddenly seem to be back. The app too often interrupts what should be a simple process of logging food with tips, prompts, and pop-ups that I’ve already seen many times.

I’d also really like better AI integration. Not having a direct integration with tools like ChatGPT or Claude is frustrating, because YAZIO’s built-in AI doesn’t seem to have enough tools to reliably break a meal down into its individual components and let me correct them precisely. In practice, it often feels less like a true nutrition assistant and more like a slicker version of Quick Add.

I’d love an option to permanently disable nutrition tips, coaching pop-ups, and other nonessential interruptions, plus a more flexible AI workflow that makes it easy to review and edit individual ingredients. YAZIO is useful, but these issues make the experience feel much more cluttered and limited than it needs to be.

One more frustration: my partner and I both use YAZIO, and we often eat the same meal or nearly the same meal, but there’s no simple way to share a logged meal or its macros between accounts. We end up entering essentially the same food twice. Being able to send or share a meal with another YAZIO user would save a lot of time and would be especially useful for couples or families tracking together.

reviews.title: Better than I thought
reviews.text:
Okay, full disclosure, when I first started using this, I disliked it so much that I stupidly canceled it and will have to renew the subscription 🙄. That's what I get for being impatient. Being post-menopausal, losing weight just almost seems impossible, and this is good for showing me my blind spots and what I may have been doing wrong. I still wish they would just show calories instead of kilajoules, because it's a hassle looking it up. I also wish that you could program it for dairy free (lactose-free is not dairy free, so that doesn't help with allergies--hence the 4 stars instead of 5. Overall, though, I can see why people like this app and since Google Health has destroyed FitBit's user-friendly interface, this is a nice, inexpensive option.

***It's a good idea to double check some of the calculations, which are sometimes much higher than other sources or doesn't take certain aspects into consideration (eg homemade almond milk has far fewer calories than commercial).

reviews.title: Can’t manually input calories anymore?
reviews.text:
UPDATED RESPONSE: I received a message from the developer in response to my review:

"Thank you for your feedback. AI camera tracking is completely optional. You can always toggle between the AI and manual tracking methods. 😉"

I need to clarify when I said “manual calorie input” I was talking about the Quick Add function. I did not mention AI Camera Tracking anywhere in my original review. To reiterate, the Quick Add function does not let you manually add calories anymore and now has a mandatory AI function in which you type out a description of your food.

I’ve been using Yazio for a couple of weeks with the goal of losing weight. I’ve been keeping to the calorie plan and logging everything I eat. I have gained a pound so I’m beginning to doubt the accuracy of the calorie tracking. 

I also feel like the navigation is a little clunky. It’s not unusable, but it’s not particularly streamlined and sometimes I have to backtrack or get to certain pages in backwards seeming ways. I would expect better for something I shelled $50 for the annual subscription.

I went ahead and got the subscription as a way to hold myself accountable but I regret doing so as there are free apps that would do exactly what this app does. I wouldn’t recommend spending the money. 

However, I do give it 4 stars because it is functional. My anecdotal evidence of not losing weight despite sticking to the plan isn’t quite enough to completely write the app off.

reviews.title: Unfortunately, I Lost One of My Favorite Apps
reviews.text:
I’m writing this review mainly because I’m trying to get the attention of the YAZIO team and support.

I’ve been using YAZIO for many years. I always loved this app, considered it one of the most convenient calorie trackers available, trusted it, and recommended it to other people.

But I honestly don’t understand what has been happening to YAZIO over the past month.

First, Quick Add stops working properly. This was one of the most useful features — I could simply enter a description, calories, and nutrients manually when I already knew the exact values. Now it either doesn’t work or tries to replace manual input with AI-generated estimates that I don’t need and that are often inaccurate.

Then products that I used to scan successfully suddenly stop being recognized by the barcode scanner. On top of that, the app keeps showing tips, suggestions, and other pop-ups that I never asked for, and sometimes there seems to be no normal way to dismiss them.

People rarely take the time to leave positive reviews unless they genuinely love a product. I had wanted to leave YAZIO a great review for a long time because I genuinely liked and trusted this app. Unfortunately, I’m leaving one star now because I don’t know how else to get the developers’ attention.

Years of positive experience have been ruined for me in a matter of weeks. Something as simple as logging my food has become frustrating, and I now have to find workarounds just to enter calories and nutrients that I already know.

Please, YAZIO team, fix the basic functionality that made this app so good in the first place. I don’t need AI to guess the calories of something when I already know the exact numbers. I need Quick Add to let me QUICKLY ADD them. I need the barcode scanner to recognize products it recognized before. And I don’t want constant tips and suggestions getting in the way of simply tracking my food.

I’m not leaving one star because I hate YAZIO. Quite the opposite — I’m leaving this review because I’ve used and trusted this app for years, and I really want it to work properly again.
